summary_paragraph: The patient, a morbidly obese male with a history of ankylosing spondylitis, hypertension, asthma, and obstructive sleep apnea, was admitted for severe right hip pain lasting nine days. He had recently been hospitalized for left hip effusion and reported frequent infections. Evaluation revealed elevated CRP without signs of systemic infection. Imaging showed mild degenerative changes in the right hip with no effusion or fracture. He was treated with a two-day course of IV methylprednisolone, resulting in significant improvement, and transitioned to a 21-day oral prednisone taper. Facial folliculitis was treated with a seven-day course of Bactrim after initial Unasyn, with clinical improvement. Trace hematuria was noted, requiring outpatient follow-up. The patient was discharged home in stable condition with plans to follow up with rheumatology and primary care for ongoing management.
problems: Ankylosing spondylitis of unspecified sites in spine
Morbid (severe) obesity due to excess calories
